text:
sam: heads up — after rolling cilium v1.24.2 to eu-west1-gpu we started seeing intermittent east-west small-packet drops for training pods, ~0.8-2% depending on burst. noticed during nightly inference runs.

alex: saw the alerts, thanks. are those drops at host->host or pod->pod level? any pattern by node or AZ?

sam: looks pod->pod across nodes, concentrated on nodes with mlx5 NICs. packet sizes ~64-256 bytes. spike lines up with rolling window when policer rules are applied.

maria: interesting — cilium 1.24 introduced policer via tc/bpf changes. could be interaction with kernel TC offload or nftables checksums. can you paste `tc -s qdisc` and `ethtool -k` from an affected host?

sam: pasted output in thread.

--- paste ---
root@gpu-node-12:~# tc -s qdisc show dev ens4
qdisc fq_codel 0: root refcnt 2 limit 10240p flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5.0ms interval 100.0ms
  backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
qdisc clsact 1: dev ens4
  Sent 1.2GiB bytes 1200000 pkt
  action stats 0x0: success 0 policer_drops 1240 overlimit 1240

root@gpu-node-12:~# ethtool -k ens4
Segmentation offload: on
Generic-receive-offload: off
Rx-checksumming: on
Tx-checksumming: on
--- end paste ---

lee: policer_drops 1240 — that's the killer. cilium inserts policer at clsact ingress/egress for service policy. with GSO/GRO and HW offloads it sometimes miscounts small packets when offload path bypasses software accounting.

alex: can we reproduce with iperf? if we craft many small UDP packets we should see same behavior. also try disabling GRO/GSO to prove offload path difference.

sam: running quick iperf3 UDP microburst: `iperf3 -c 10.0.3.45 -u -b 500M -l 128 -t 30` shows 1.6% lost and tc shows policer_drops incrementing.

maria: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback cilium to previous minor (1.23.x) 2) tweak policer config to be less aggressive for small packets 3) disable host offload (GRO/GSO) temporarily 4) apply kernel patch/workaround that upstream discussed.

lee: rolling back is safest short-term. but we need a repro to file with cilium and NIC vendor. rollback window?

sam: can do a canary rollback of the daemonset on 2 nodes in eu-west1 to validate. planning to patch two k8s nodes tonight at 21:30 UTC.

oncall-bot: incident created — INC-2145: `cilium-police-eu-west1-small-packet-drops`. Severity: P2. Paging eng-infra oncall.

alex: while rolling back, let's collect tcpdumps (small-pkt samples) and skb metadata from `bpftool` where possible. also get `nstat` and `ethtool -S` for mlx5 counters.

sam: collecting dumps now: `tcpdump -i cilium_host -s 128 -w /tmp/smallpkt.pcap 'udp and (len <= 256)'` and `bpftool prog show` output attached.

maria: for a reproducible minimal test we should try toggling `enable-legacy-policer: true/false` in cilium configmap (if present) and measure. there was a commit that changed policer->bpf enforcement in 1.24.2.

lee: also check SR-IOV/VF drivers — some NICs have checksum offload quirks that flip length/segmentation flags. that combined with clsact/policer could cause misclassification and drop counters.

sam: quick mitigation applied: set `GRO` off on ens4 on affected nodes via `ethtool -K ens4 gro off` — after that tc policer_drops stopped increasing during the iperf microburst test.

alex: good sign — points to offload accounting. but GRO off hurts throughput slightly. we can leave toggle for now while troubleshooting deeper.

maria: open a cilium issue with pcap, bpftool, tc output + kernel version + ethtool -k. also cc Mellanox support (link ticket) if NIC-specific. I can draft it.

sam: created issue #CILIUM-2145 with logs and pcap. tagging @maria and @lee.

devops-bot: deploy rollback started for cilium-ds in eu-west1-zone-a (pods terminating: 4).

lee: after rollback confirm `tc -s qdisc` shows policer_drops not incrementing and run the same iperf test. if stable, we can promote rollback cluster-wide and schedule a slower upgrade with additional gating.

sam: rollback results: after reverting to 1.23.7 the microburst test shows 0.1% loss (baseline) and policer_drops=0. Rolling back cluster now.

alex: follow-ups: 1) add a gating test for small-packet microbursts to our upgrade CI 2) add quick toggle to nodejs training infra to disable GRO if we detect policer drops 3) coordinate with cilium maintainers on a fix timeline.

maria: agree. I'll draft a postmortem note with timeline and mitigation and recommend we avoid wide 1.24 rollouts until upstream confirms fix.

sam: thanks all — keeping this thread open till rollback fully done and ticket updates arrive. :thumbsup:
